question: A can do a task in 18 days, and B in 9 days. After working together for 4 days, A leaves. How many more days will B take to complete the remaining work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 18 and 9 = 18 (Total Work)

⇒ A = 1 unit/day, B = 2 units/day

⇒ Together = 3 units/day

⇒ In 4 days = 3 × 4 = 12 units

⇒ Remaining = 18 − 12 = 6 units

⇒ B alone time = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 days

**∴ Answer = 3 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A completes work in 18 days

B completes work in 9 days

Calculations:

 Efficiency (Work/day)
 
 

 A

 18

⇒ Work done in 4 days = 3 × 4 = 12

⇒ Remaining work = 18 − 12 = 6

⇒ B's efficiency = 2 units/day

⇒ Time taken by B = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 days

**∴ Remaining time = 3 days**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**LCM Method:** Converts total work into integer units for easy calculation.

**Efficiency Concept:** Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

**Work Left:** Remaining Work = Total Work − Completed Work

**Individual Work:** After one leaves, remaining work is done by the other alone.
